pillars.note: The objective is the burning conditions of materials in microgravity as a function of material properties, to build flammability maps: the prevention pillar. The ISA text also says that flames kept burning without air flow, and the cessation of ventilation is an established step in putting out spacecraft fires; that bears on suppression practice but is not encoded. Pillar is the curator's classification, not a source statement.

evidence.quote: The BRE flight program seeks to establish the burning conditions in a quiescent microgravity ambient in terms of material properties.
This could enable the Cone Calorimeter (NASA Test 2) test as a basis for establishing flammability maps for real materials.
BRE yielded important data relevant to spacecraft fire safety.

nominal_atmosphere.note: As-run statements: flames were tested at 21 percent O2 and 14.7 psia, 27 percent and 10.2 psia, and 34 percent and 8.2 psia (p. 18; the plan on p. 5 gives 26.5 percent for the middle pair), and with O2 up to 40 percent (p. 20); 'more of the testing was conducted at roughly atmospheric pressure' with elevated O2. The min/max is an envelope of those conditions and the pairing is not representable: do not combine 40 percent O2 with 8.2 psia or 34 percent with 14.7 psia. The experimental table gives O2 per test day and no pressure.
